title: Modern Chinese Grammar
full_title: Modern Chinese Grammar: Words, Phrases and Sentences
tagline: What grammar is, parts of speech, function words, phrases, sentence constituents, sentence patterns and types, special constructions, complex sentences, and faulty sentences
summary: Chinese has almost no inflection, so its grammar lies in word order and function words, which native speakers use effortlessly but rarely analyse. This course describes the grammar of modern Chinese: the parts of speech and the function words, how phrases are built, the constituents and patterns of sentences, special constructions such as the 把 and 被 sentences, complex sentences, and how to find and correct faulty sentences.

chapters.title: What grammar is
chapters.summary: Grammatical units and relations, the characteristics of Chinese grammar, and the main systems of description since the *Mashi Wentong* of 1898.

chapters.title: Parts of speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, verbs, adjectives, numerals and classifiers, pronouns and adverbs, how they are told apart by their grammatical function, and words that belong to two classes.

chapters.title: Function words
chapters.summary: Prepositions, conjunctions, the structural particles 的, 地 and 得, the aspect particles 了, 着 and 过, and modal particles.

chapters.title: Phrases
chapters.summary: Subject–predicate, verb–object, modifier–head, verb–complement and coordinate phrases, and analysing phrases layer by layer.

chapters.title: Sentence constituents
chapters.summary: Subject, predicate, object, attributive, adverbial and complement, with the many kinds of complement that Chinese uses.

chapters.title: Sentence patterns and types
chapters.summary: Subject–predicate and subjectless sentences, and statements, questions, commands and exclamations.

chapters.title: Special constructions
chapters.summary: The 把 and 被 sentences, existential sentences, serial-verb and pivotal constructions, and comparative sentences.

chapters.title: Complex sentences
chapters.summary: Coordinate and subordinate relations between clauses, the connectives that mark them, multi-layered complex sentences, and the run-on style (流水句) of Chinese.

chapters.title: Finding and correcting faulty sentences
chapters.summary: Mismatched constituents, wrong word order, missing or redundant parts, misused connectives and ambiguity, and a method for correcting them.
